lines: Ahh. A shell. I wondered who it would be today. Hello again, {player}.
Yes, it's me, your principal, out on a field trip. The warm rocks in these gardens are excellent.
{player}: Why do I have a SHELL? And why does Pip say their wings feel like flippers?
Magic, my dear {player}. The Void is a planet that thinks, and sometimes it dreams. And some days, everyone wakes up a different version of themselves.
People here do love their magic. A bit too much, if you ask me. Magic for breakfast, magic for lunch, magic for brushing your teeth.
You didn't choose your shell. Most of the time, we don't get to choose. Your body, your brain, the planet you wake up on.
But every version of you has purpose and value. Even this slow, shelly one. Especially this one, perhaps.
Now. Since you have a shell, you'll understand the little lake turtles. The Void's turtles use THINGS as their shells, and nobody has ever let them choose their own.
Today is their Independence Day. Find them three things that could be a home: a teacup, a bucket, a flower pot. Then let THEM choose.
Ahh. A shell. I wondered who it would be today.
Don't be frightened. I am the Wizard Lizard: principal of the castle school, friend of the Seer, keeper of rules, and very fond of naps on warm rocks.

A teacup at the Market's south end, a bucket on the dock, a flower pot by the greenhouse. And then: let them choose.
Don't choose for them. That's the whole point. Very important. I'll be napping on this rock.

They chose? Each one, all by themselves? Wonderful. Wonderful!
That's independence, {player}. Not getting to choose everything. Just getting to choose something, and having it respected.
Now, your shell. The magic's wearing off. You'll be your own self again by the time you reach the portal.
But I can leave the shell with you, if you like. It's yours now. You earned it.
A fine choice. It suits you. Slow and steady, as they say.

choice.text: I'll take it off for now.
lines: Also a fine choice. I'll pop it in your wardrobe. Wear it whenever you like.
Why does the planet do it, you ask? Why turtles, why today?
...Just because? Some things are just because. Off you go.
(The Wizard Lizard looks up from a very tall stack of papers.)
{player}! The turtles' helper! Welcome to my school. Didn't I say? I'm the principal here.
Principals come in all shapes, my dear. Mine happens to be scaly. Very good at sitting on warm rocks, which is most of the job.
This school has only three rules. One: every version of you is welcome here. Every single one.
Two: no running in the halls. Unless something's chasing you. Then run.
Three: naps are allowed. Encouraged, even.
If you ever need a wise word, my door is open. If it's shut, I'm napping. Knock anyway.
And if you want to know what's coming, don't ask me. Ask my old friend the Seer, up in the Observatory. She has a lantern for that sort of thing.

rotate: Tiny, Splash and Pebble have been showing off their shells to everyone. Even the fish.
Every version of anything has purpose and value. I tell the rocks that too. They take it very well.
(The Wizard Lizard is asleep on his warm rock. He's smiling.)
Principal's tip of the day: if a problem looks too big, look at it from a warm rock. Everything's smaller from a warm rock.
The halls are quiet today. I like quiet. Quiet is where good ideas sit down.
My friend the Seer says the stars are very busy this week. She says that every week.
Rule one, {player}. Every version of you is welcome here. I like to say it out loud now and then, in case anyone forgot.
Mm? Oh, hello. I was resting my eyes. Principals need a lot of rest.
